record.paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
record.original_question: Can the same algebraic polynomial method for constructing nuclear density functionals from finite configuration-mixing models and polynomial density constraints be applied to nuclear cluster-model calculations?

evidence.quote: Another interesting question is, can this algebraic method be used for the cluster model? We have again preliminary results which are optimistic. But they are also ... too preliminary.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a finite-dimensional configuration-mixing framework for a self-bound many-body fermion system (such as an atomic nucleus). Suppose one has a finite family of trial many-body states {|Φ_i⟩}_{i=1}^N, each producing a one-body density ρ_i(r), and one forms mixed states by superposition with coefficients that are determined by enforcing a finite set of polynomial constraints on the total density ρ(r) (for instance, constraints of the form ∫ P_k(r) ρ(r) d^3r = c_k for prescribed polynomials P_k and values c_k). Within this setting, one can construct an energy density functional E[ρ] purely algebraically: the functional is obtained by eliminating the mixing parameters from the polynomial density constraints, yielding E[ρ] as an algebraic (polynomial) function of moments of ρ. Call this construction the "algebraic polynomial method" for energy density functionals.

Question. Does there exist an analogous algebraic polynomial construction in the context of nuclear cluster models — i.e., many-body trial states built from a finite set of pre-formed cluster substructures (such as α-particle clusters) with relative coordinates and antisymmetrization between clusters — such that:
(i) the cluster-model trial states play the role of the finite configuration-mixing basis;
(ii) a finite set of polynomial constraints on the total one-body density (or on cluster-collective coordinates) plays the role of the density constraints; and
(iii) elimination of the mixing/cluster parameters yields a closed-form polynomial energy density functional E[ρ] reproducing the cluster-model energies?

Determine whether such an algebraic polynomial construction of an energy density functional from cluster-model calculations exists in general, and if so describe the class of cluster models and polynomial density constraints for which it is well-defined.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of whether the algebraic polynomial construction of energy density functionals from finite configuration-mixing/polynomial-density-constraint setups can be extended to nuclear cluster models. While constrained DFT is used to study cluster phenomena (e.g., α-cluster configurations via density-constrained Hartree-Fock) and there is recent work on cluster models within DFT frameworks, none of the located sources establish (or refute) a general algebraic polynomial construction of the desired type. Status appears unresolved in publicly accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Cluster model of 12C in the density functional theory framework
status_evidence.snippet: Constrained density functional theory can be employed to investigate cluster phenomena, where proton and neutron densities are generated from the placement of alpha particles geometrically and then used in a density constrained Hartree-Fock calculation.
status_evidence.claim: DFT-based cluster-model calculations exist but use density-constrained HF rather than an explicit algebraic polynomial elimination construction.

status_evidence.title: Building surrogate models of nuclear density functional theory
status_evidence.snippet: Surrogate models of nuclear density functional theory using Gaussian processes and autoencoders.
status_evidence.claim: Recent EDF construction work focuses on machine-learning surrogates rather than algebraic polynomial constructions from cluster models.
